text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Kenya's ruling party Kenya African National Union says it will not have dialogue with National Convention Executive Council or National Convention Assembly on constitutional reforms as they are non-elective bodies.
- Britain reviewing aid to Kenya after political unrest on July 7 in which nine people died in pro-reform rallies.
- Police arrest 18 more Rwandans, bringing total number arrested to 180.
- Opposition leaders and pro-reform groups present proposals on constitutional reforms to Head of Public Service and Secretary to the Cabinet Fares Kuindwa.
- At least 4,000 secondary school teachers will get salary arrears backdated to July 1, 1996, along with their July salary.
- Opposition party FORD-Kenya disowns all its members who oppose dialogue on constitutional reforms with President Moi.
- Opposition members of parliament disown National Convention Executive Council and accuse lobby of hijacking reform initiatives.
- Government signs 2.6 billion shilling contract with Canadian company allowing firm to explore for oil.
- Militant campaign for constitutional reforms has been financed by a number of Western nations with funds channelled through reform lobbyists and some Non-Governmental Organisations.
